design.title: DBT explicit selection fail-closed policy
design.rationale: Preview and readiness now consume one DBT execution projection. An absent selection may derive workspace scope, while a non-empty selection with no executable DBT resource is rejected before Preview and is rejected independently by server authority.

design.title: DBT execution selection intent integrity
design.rationale: CollectCanvasExecutionSelection remains the single query seam. Workspace fallback and explicit empty intent are distinct states; gestures and graph lifecycle updates preserve the complete requested set; unavailable roots remain visible; and only RecoverCanvasExecutionSelection may explicitly discard or replace that intent.

design.title: DBT execution selection recovery
design.rationale: Execution-selection recovery is explicit and fail-closed. Refresh analysis produces a success receipt only when the authority query succeeds and the owning context accepts the returned projection as usable; DBT requires fresh analysis.

design.title: Require composition-owned route dependencies
design.rationale: StartRun and workspace-context routes consume composition-selected observability and adapter registries; routes no longer select Null Objects or deployment defaults, while the deterministic run-id generator remains a bounded test seam.

design.title: Consolidate API production reachability architecture guard
design.rationale: Extend the existing ApplyArchitectureDependencyBoundaryGate rail to classify every API source from production and test roots, model supported runtime profiles semantically, reject new test-only or fake reachability, and retire the drifting package-local guard without a filename allowlist.

design.title: Propagate nested switch-path exits
design.rationale: Reuse switch-path abrupt-completion semantics for predecessors inside nested blocks so break and continue make later profile evidence unreachable without broadening the guard into a general control-flow graph.

design.title: Track directed abrupt switch completion
design.rationale: Model normal and directed abrupt completion for statically selected switch paths so an unlabeled break completes its own switch while labeled breaks and continues propagate to their actual enclosing target; unknown selection remains conservative.

design.title: Consolidate API production reachability architecture guard
design.rationale: Extend the existing ApplyArchitectureDependencyBoundaryGate rail to classify every API source from production and test roots, model supported runtime profiles semantically, reject new test-only or fake reachability, and retire the drifting package-local guard without a filename allowlist.

design.title: Harden API production reachability semantics after Fowler QA
design.rationale: Separate runtime and type reachability, derive supported profile evidence from AST branch semantics, attribute conditional and Null Object profiles to concrete modules, reject type-only and unused-value fake reachability, and preserve transitive test-support export evidence in the existing ApplyArchitectureDependencyBoundaryGate rail.

design.title: Bind API reachability evidence to executable scopes and type retention
design.rationale: Make Dependency Cruiser dependencyTypes authoritative for runtime traversal, retain meaningfully used production type contracts on a separate production-type-support axis, and require enabled providers and dynamic imports to share the guarded function, class, or imported composition function call path.

design.title: Prove enabled profiles on executable call paths
design.rationale: Reject dead constant branches and uncalled same-class methods as supported deployment evidence while retaining the existing runtime/type reachability axes and command rail.

design.title: Anchor profile evidence to reachable guards and composition entrypoints
design.rationale: Reject unreachable guards, negated constant target branches, terminated blocks, and dead reconciler orchestrators while preserving the existing report and rail.

design.title: Anchor profile evidence to live composition roots
design.rationale: Require deployment guards and enabled targets to be statically reachable through executable composition roots, including literal and short-circuit control flow, and require reconciler evidence to traverse its create entrypoint.

design.title: Prove callback and factory-product consumption
design.rationale: Replace inferred callback and factory edges with parameter-invocation and consumed-product proof, and extend static flow truth to cast literals and terminating switches while preserving the existing rail and report.

design.title: Exclude statically unselected switch clauses
design.rationale: Extend the existing executable-path proof to model statically selected switch entry clauses, default selection, fallthrough, break, and termination so inline targets, invoked callbacks, and consumed factory products cannot prove a deployment profile from an unselected case.

design.title: Guarantee push comparison base availability
design.rationale: Fetch github.event.before explicitly for push-triggered architecture checks so a shallow checkout can compare multi-commit deliveries; retain PR and workflow-dispatch baselines and the existing no-merge-base direct-tree fallback.

design.title: Bind push reachability diff to pre-push SHA
design.rationale: Use the pull-request base SHA for PRs and github.event.before for pushes so changed-only orphan and test-support enforcement evaluates the actual delivered delta on every mandatory workflow trigger.

design.title: Remap API artifact resolution authority
design.rationale: The manifest resolver was retired because planner owns manifest derivation; retain the real run-context artifact adapter and align every current architecture fact to its surviving implementation and tests.

design.title: Remap API run-context artifact authority
design.rationale: The planner-owned manifest derivation replaced the deleted API manifest resolver; remap the surviving component, relation, contract, port, evidence, and test facts to the run-context artifact adapter without compatibility aliases.

design.title: Align canonical run-context artifact authority
design.rationale: Planner owns manifest graph derivation; the API retains only the engine-owned run-context resolver port adapter. Align component, relation, contract, port, evidence, and test authority to that surviving boundary.

design.title: Disposition inert API implementations and test seams
design.rationale: Preserve the explicit disabled-observability Null Object, require the already-composed StartRun telemetry ports, and retire only reachability-proved duplicate adapters, orphan bridges, and production-only test seams without changing HTTP or Run semantics.

design.title: Close residual API test-only exports
design.rationale: Complete the generated export disposition by removing redundant test-only re-exports and a test-only compatibility constant while retaining their production-owned types, policies, and reconciler behavior through existing modules.

design.title: Remove current links to superseded architecture documents
design.rationale: Five active canonical pages still link to four lifecycle-superseded documents; current navigation must use the existing DB-first projection while historical evidence remains byte-unchanged.

design.title: Verify GitHub Actions evidence before recording CI origin
design.rationale: Fail closed unless a concrete successful GitHub Actions job belongs to the canonical repository and current commit.

design.title: DB-first document and evidence reconciliation
design.rationale: Replace current local architecture assertions through hash-matched DB dispositions, correct component ownership, require executable evidence provenance, and preserve explicit on-demand publication without migration or compatibility state.

design.title: DB-first document evidence and recovery reconciliation
design.rationale: Replace current local architecture assertions through hash-matched DB dispositions, preserve those DB facts across clean CI recovery, correct generated ownership, require executable evidence provenance, and retain explicit on-demand publication without migration or compatibility state.

design.title: DB-first current document and ownership reconciliation
design.rationale: Complete the approved DB-first lifecycle and evidence model by correcting the four exact generated ownership components, recording executable proof, and preserving explicit publication semantics without migration or compatibility state.

design.title: Retire stale API component test authority after independent QA
design.rationale: Independent Fowler QA proved that three retired API test files remained required architecture.component_test facts after ownership reconciliation; retire them through an explicit audited DB command and guard their absence.

design.title: Close DB-first product truth and evidence gaps after independent Fowler QA
design.rationale: Close all seven independent-QA P1 findings through exact-hash authority, audited retirement, design/source-bound latest evidence, DB-owned observability truth, and on-demand generated navigation without rewriting history.

design.title: Make documentation index generation lifecycle DB-first
design.rationale: Explicit docs:sync currently reintroduces lifecycle-superseded documents by enumerating the filesystem; generated navigation must filter through Planning DB without adding a registry or implicit generation.

design.title: Make documentation index generation lifecycle DB-first
design.rationale: Explicit docs:sync must filter current Markdown navigation through Planning DB, exclude superseded pages and ADRs, preserve archive navigation, and never add a local registry or implicit generation.

design.title: Resolve retired documentation links in disposable publication
design.rationale: Preserve historical source bytes while making active publication references resolve to immutable Git evidence under Planning DB lifecycle authority.

design.title: Canvas backlog component integrity readiness projection
design.rationale: Canvas UX database backlog rows include virtual component boundaries that are intentionally not implemented yet. Integrity must not require maturity tests for proposed/review backlog components because that incentivizes fake evidence; active approved/implemented/drift components still fail when required maturity evidence is missing.

design.title: Canvas bottom drawer actionable read model
design.rationale: The bottom operational drawer owns readiness, runs and execution preview diagnostics. Canvas route posture is now projected through a presenter read model, while OperationalDrawerPanels remain presentation-only primitives that render actions and status summaries from the contribution contract.

design.title: Canvas transform column metadata workbench projection
design.rationale: DBT model nodes and DVT SQL transforms are both transform-role nodes. Their contextual workbench must project upstream source columns, types, nullability, source references and selected-column state when the node itself has not recorded output columns yet. The column projection therefore belongs to InspectCanvasNodeProperties instead of a DVT-only helper.

design.title: Canvas component registry drift guard
design.rationale: Canvas UI work must be component-first. The registry drift guard compares DB-owned governed source files with the DB-owned frontend component registry so unmapped Canvas files, duplicate file owners and legacy palette surfaces are visible before UI implementation proceeds.

design.title: Canvas component registry ownership reconciliation
design.rationale: Canvas component ownership is explicit: node-card presentation files belong to their focused UI components and the authoring selector has one DVT owner.

design.title: Canvas context-menu echo consumption repair
design.rationale: The Canvas context menu suppresses browser echo events after a pane context-menu open. Review evidence showed the document pointer echo could be consumed without clearing the pending echo state, causing a later click at the original context point to be ignored. The presenter now consumes that pending state exactly when the document echo is handled, preserving intentional outside-click dismissal.

design.title: Canvas context-menu echo repair canonical rail owner
design.rationale: The echo repair initially recorded a second active ResolveCanvasContextMenu declaration with a different owner. The canonical rail is already active under CanvasNodeContextMenuView, so the repair reuses that owner and leaves command_query_rail_vocabulary_query with zero exact_duplicate findings.

design.title: Canvas context-menu echo repair duplicate rail retirement
design.rationale: The echo repair rail was an implementation patch for the canonical ResolveCanvasContextMenu rail, not a separate product query. Retiring the alias keeps feature history while restoring a single active command/query vocabulary row.

design.title: Canvas context menu shell layer
design.rationale: CanvasShell owned the context-menu presenter and rendered the context-menu view directly as a loose sibling in the shell group. The professional canvas surface needs a named layer component so menu hosting, pointer-event policy, and shell integration are separated from shell orchestration.

design.title: Canvas context-menu view-model canonical rail reuse
design.rationale: The view-model extraction is a presenter refactor under ResolveCanvasContextMenu. Retiring the slice-local rail prevents duplicate vocabulary while preserving database symbol and validation evidence.

design.title: Canvas command/query rail drift guard
design.rationale: Canvas UI implementation must not create duplicate action names for the same product intent. Canvas UX DB records now resolve through this guard before UI slices implement menus, workbenches, drawers, preview, source import, project exploration or run actions.

design.title: Canvas command/query rail vocabulary normalization
design.rationale: Canvas UX records must use canonical command/query rail vocabulary before graph, shell, source import, node workbench, SQL workbench, project explorer, manual export or browser-proof UI slices are implemented.

design.title: Warehouse source connection identity for graph node cards
design.rationale: Imported warehouse source cards should expose the warehouse connection family, such as Postgres, instead of leaking generated database identifiers as the visible source identity. ImportWarehouseSources persists the catalog-owned connection identity and GraphNodeTitlePresentation renders it as the card title vocabulary.

design.title: Canvas node port handle presentation boundary
design.rationale: CanvasNodeShell must compose presentation components instead of embedding React Flow handle markup and styling. The extracted CanvasNodePortHandle keeps port rendering under the GraphNodeCard component owner while leaving DBT/DVT card strategy behavior outside the shell.

design.title: Canonical selected-node presentation truth and contextual surface coordination
design.rationale:
Current state: GraphNodeCard derives declared columns from node metadata; NodeWorkbench silently substitutes inherited transform inputs; CanvasViewport owns independent toolbar and health states while workbench visibility lives in shell state. This produces contradictory counts and competing surfaces.

Target state: CanonicalNode + graph context -> CanvasNodePresentationTruth -> GraphNodeCardStrategy and NodePropertiesReadModel -> passive views. CanvasNodeContextSurfaceCoordinator accepts node selection, health, workbench, code, removal, and dismissal events and exposes at most one transient contextual surface. File-backed code is represented as workspace-file authority, never as missing inline SQL. Copy is supplied by the locale catalog rather than embedded in read models.

Remaining contradiction: dbtAuthoringFieldsModel and canvasDbtWorkspaceArtifacts independently derive model SQL while CanvasNodePresentationTruth reports pathless authored models as unavailable. Target correction: one DbtModelArtifactProjection supplies generated or authored SQL with explicit provenance to artifact generation, card truth, and workbench inspection. DbtModelCodeAuthoringSection adapts the existing ConfigureCanvasDbtNode command and owns no projection policy.

Closeout: one pure DBT model artifact projection now supplies General, Code, Preview, and workspace materialization. The Code workbench adapts edits through ConfigureCanvasDbtNode, generated and authored provenance remain explicit, passive empty content is suppressed when the contextual editor owns the section, and strict live browser proof exercises the complete warehouse-source to project-file roundtrip.

design.title: Canvas node workbench DBT test rows read model
design.rationale: nodePropertiesReadModel owned generic node sections plus DBT-specific test parsing, assertion wording, selection state and last-run projection. Extracting DBT test rows to a pure read model keeps the coordinator small, makes DBT test semantics directly testable, and preserves InspectCanvasNodeProperties as the owning query rail.

design.title: Canvas node workbench draft reconciliation controller
design.rationale:
Current state: CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel composes tabs and read models while also tracking authoritative node revisions, dirty form state, tag text, cancellation, and node switches. That gives the presentation component a second reason to change and makes an explicitly empty SQL draft vulnerable to authoritative refreshes.

Target state: useCanvasNodeWorkbenchDraftController owns the deterministic UI-state transition between authoritative CanonicalNode snapshots and one editable CanvasInspectorNodeDraft. CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel consumes its controller port. Persistence remains exclusively behind ConfigureCanvasDbtNode/ConfigureCanvasDvtNode; no new CQ rail is introduced for local presentation state.

Closeout: CanvasNodeWorkbenchDraftController now owns the authoritative-snapshot to transient-draft state machine. CanvasInspectorAuthoringSection is a controlled form leaf with exclusive source ownership. CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel composes both without owning draft state. The controller has no CQ rail because it has no application effect; the form references the existing ConfigureCanvasDbtNode and ConfigureCanvasDvtNode commands.

design.title: Canvas node workbench section-scoped authoring
design.rationale: The Node Workbench already projected columns and SQL through InspectCanvasNodeProperties, but editable DVT transform controls were rendered as one general authoring block. This slice scopes authoring controls to the section that owns the user intent: selected input columns in Columns and transform SQL in Code.

design.title: Canvas node workbench source metadata projection
design.rationale: Imported warehouse sources carried catalog columns but dropped source row counts before they reached the persisted graph draft. DVT transform column selection also lived in a view-local helper even though NodeWorkbench and DVT authoring need the same vocabulary. This slice preserves catalog-owned source statistics and moves the selectable-column projection into the NodeWorkbench read-model boundary.

design.title: Canvas node workbench strategy sections
design.rationale: CanvasSurfaceStrategy already declared DBT and DVT node workbench sections, but NodePropertiesTabs still chose primary tabs through a component-local constant. The slice introduces a pure strategy-to-read-model translator so DBT/DVT surface policies choose workbench sections without embedding domain decisions in JSX presentation.

design.title: Canvas review comment closeout rail alignment
design.rationale: Review feedback identified two database read-model drifts: duplicate canonical command/query rail sources were hidden by same-owner counting, and AuthorCanvasGraphEdge local overlays could be rebuilt from imported rails instead of the active DB-local rail. The fix keeps canonical duplicates visible while preserving local feature overlays as the active authority.

design.title: Canvas surface strategy sink workbench section
design.rationale: DVT declared a sink workbench section in the canvas surface strategy, but the section translator dropped it and the editable sink target lived inside the generic General section. This migration records the explicit section vocabulary, the InspectCanvasNodeProperties sink read model, and the component evidence proving DVT sink target editing lives in a dedicated contextual workbench tab.

design.title: Canvas top bar compact run status indicator
design.rationale: The top bar renders only the compact run readiness summary from the bottom operational drawer contribution while Problems and Preview retain actionable detail.

design.title: Canvas UX database acceptance catalog
design.rationale: TAREA.TXT defines UX, database, product, implementation and validation acceptance criteria. Those criteria must be Planning DB records before Canvas P0 UI slices can claim completion.

design.title: Canvas UX professional reference catalog
design.rationale: The current TAREA.TXT specification requires professional UX references, mandatory UX/DB vocabulary, component surfaces, command/query specs, tests and export posture to be queryable in Planning DB before further Canvas UI implementation.

design.title: Canvas UX database specification persistence
design.rationale: The Canvas-first redesign must not proceed from raw Markdown or route-local UI vocabulary. TAREA.TXT is persisted as typed Planning DB records so UI slices can reuse one vocabulary, one component map, and one command/query rail map.

design.title: Canvas viewport component slice boundaries
design.rationale: CanvasViewport mixed React Flow presentation, CSS token resolution, imperative viewport lifecycle, and context-menu presenter wiring. The component slice separates presentation from UI logic so later TAREA.TXT work can evolve graph templates, palette tokens, and viewport lifecycle without editing the route-facing orchestrator.

design.title: Code working-tree automatic synchronization
design.rationale: Code edits synchronize automatically through the existing revision-guarded SaveWorkspaceFileContent command. The UI exposes honest synchronized, modified, syncing, conflict, failed, and read-only posture without a Save action or a false Git stage, commit, push, or remote-sync claim.

design.title: Code working-tree strict live vertical
design.rationale: The governed live runner now proves DBT authoring, persisted preview, Start Run, Monaco autosynchronization through SaveWorkspaceFileContent, authoritative GetWorkspaceFileContent reads, and browser reopen without workspace-file intercepts, direct edited-content seeding, or a Save UI.

design.title: Command/query rail same-owner feature evidence rollup
design.rationale: Feature mechanization can record several feature rows against one canonical rail and DDD owner. The effective rail read model must preserve those feature/source references while counting them as one canonical declaration so Canvas workbench slices do not create false duplicate rail blockers.

design.title: Retire removed Canvas context menu primitive authority
design.rationale: Retire the removed PRIMITIVES component and its containment relation while preserving the surviving VIEW authority and historical state.

design.title: DBT graph model SQL authority containment
design.rationale:
A graph-draft Canvas and Project Code currently expose two writable representations of the same DBT model SQL. Preview reads the latest workspace-file revision immediately before writing, so an external or Project Code edit can be accepted as the expected revision and silently overwritten. Containment makes generated graph-owned SQL self-identifying, preflights every model SQL artifact before publication, and presents graph-owned project files as read-only without changing file-authoritative DBT projects.

Closeout: graph-derived DBT model SQL now carries a payload-integrity marker, all artifacts complete preflight before the first write, and every save retains the exact revision observed during preflight. A newer unmarked or malformed model file stops Preview without writing any artifact. Project Code renders graph-owned files read-only, while file-authoritative DBT projects retain revision-guarded editing. Protected browser evidence exercises the node Code affordance, Preview, Run, Project Code, an external file edit, and byte-for-byte preservation after the rejected Preview.

Upgrade correction: an unmarked divergent model file cannot be classified safely from bytes alone. Preview must expose an explicit replacement confirmation bound to the observed file revision and proposed graph payload. Cancellation preserves every file; a changed file or graph invalidates the authorization; malformed managed markers remain non-replaceable.

Pre-marker closeout: divergent unmarked SQL now requires a user decision bound to the exact observed file SHA-256 and proposed managed-content SHA-256. Cancellation performs no write, stale confirmation reopens the decision, malformed managed markers remain blocked, and the protected browser flow proves preservation followed by explicit adoption.

design.title: Mutually exclusive dbt project authoring authority
design.owner: Web / API / Project Workspace I/O / dbt Integration
design.rationale: Graph-authored and file-backed dbt projects cannot both own semantic nodes and edges. WorkspaceGraphAuthoringDraft.v1 remains graph-draft authority; file-backed Canvas requires a separate authority binding, server projection, and route-local layout.

design.title: Web Canvas field component canonicalization

design.title: Web Canvas parent leaf closure
design.rationale: After adding Canvas harness leaves, graph viewport, node workbench, and shell main panel became composite parents with residual direct file claims. This design closes that drift with presentation, panel, and architecture-test leaves.

design.title: Web Canvas leaf component ownership mapping
design.rationale: SYS-WEB-VIEW-CANVAS still owned concrete Canvas files after its first subdivision. This design records focused leaf components for harnesses, overlay presentation, and authoring field tests so component-profile can answer which files and tests belong to each Canvas subcomponent.

design.title: Web Canvas leaf component relation mapping
design.rationale: New Canvas leaf components need explicit architecture.component, contains relations, and required test evidence. CanvasNodeWorkbenchOverlay.tsx is now tracked and functional, so the previous deprecated architecture row is reactivated instead of left as a ghost component.

design.title: Web Canvas modularized test evidence mapping
design.rationale: The modularized Canvas leaves must be queryable with concrete test evidence. This design attaches executable tests to the newly created ownership leaves without changing their component authority.

design.title: Web Canvas modularized test evidence leaf collision closure
design.rationale: Some historical test identifiers are already reserved outside the architecture-evidence read model. This design records collision-free leaf-specific test evidence for the remaining Canvas modularization components.

design.title: Web Canvas modularized test leaf ownership mapping
design.rationale: Recent Canvas modularization added functional tests and split inspector tabs into runtime plus tests. This design records leaf ownership for those real files, keeps old or nonfunctional surfaces eligible for deprecation, and avoids runtime/test duplicate components.

design.title: Web Canvas node context-menu leaf authority
design.rationale: SYS-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-CONTEXT-MENU-VIEW was a real implemented concern, but its parent component did not exist in the unit tree and its model/test files were still owned by the broad Canvas component bucket. Reparent the leaf under the active Canvas context-menu core, keep ResolveCanvasContextMenu as the canonical query rail, and record file, test, port, and maturity evidence.

design.title: Separate Canvas node context-menu presentation
design.rationale: CanvasNodeShell owns the React Flow shell and gestures; CanvasNodeContextMenuView owns the rendered node menu template so node workbench sections are not duplicated as context-menu actions.

design.title: Web Canvas node properties tabs split test reconciliation
design.rationale: Parallel Web work replaced the monolithic NodePropertiesTabs.test.tsx evidence with focused overflow, primary-section, and section-content tests. This design keeps SYS-WEB-CANVAS-INSPECTOR-NODE-PROPERTIES-TABS-TESTS as the canonical test component, maps the real tracked files, and records the removed monolithic path as deprecated ownership evidence.

design.title: Web Canvas node workbench duplicate component resolution
design.rationale: SYS-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL duplicated the existing SYS-WEB-CANVAS-INSPECTOR-PANEL responsibility for InspectorPanel.tsx. The fix keeps the inspector shell component, reparents it under NodeWorkbench, creates a separate fields leaf for DBT/DVT editors, and marks the duplicate panel split as retired/deprecated.

design.title: Deduplicate Canvas node workbench overlay panel relation
design.rationale: The Canvas node workbench overlay had both a canonical dependency on SYS-WEB-CANVAS-INSPECTOR-PANEL and a legacy dependency on the superseded SYS-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL phantom component. Because architecture.component_relation has no deprecated state, this migration keeps the canonical overlay-to-inspector relation and removes the obsolete overlay-to-panel alias.

design.title: Restore active Canvas node workbench panel after retirement merge
design.rationale: The merge brings tracked CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel source and test files from main, while the retirement slice can still leave SYS-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL deprecated and its DB-local feature manifest deleted in local databases. The final authority is the implemented Canvas-owned panel, with the historical retirement records retained only as superseded drift evidence.

design.title: Make Canvas node workbench panel ownership effective
design.rationale: The node workbench panel has a real CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel.tsx source, but previous imported phantom-retirement rows can still surface as deprecated unless the DB-local component definition, architecture rows, tests, and observability are reasserted after import.

design.title: Neutralize Canvas node workbench panel feature manifest rehydration
design.rationale: An external feature-manifest rehydration restored InspectCanvasNodeProperties with source_path apps/web/src/app/views/canvas/CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel.tsx. The file is not tracked in this branch, so the rail is removed and the panel remains audit-only deprecated evidence.

design.title: Retire Canvas node workbench panel feature manifest
design.rationale: Superseded by PLANNING-DB-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL-ACTIVE-MERGE-RECONCILIATION-20260619 because tracked CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel source and test files now exist.

design.title: Guard final Canvas node workbench panel retirement
design.rationale: Superseded by PLANNING-DB-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL-ACTIVE-MERGE-RECONCILIATION-20260619 because tracked CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel source and test files now exist.

design.title: Neutralize parallel Canvas node workbench panel reactivation
design.rationale: Superseded by PLANNING-DB-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL-ACTIVE-MERGE-RECONCILIATION-20260619 because tracked CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel source and test files now exist.

design.title: Retire phantom Canvas node workbench panel reactivation
design.rationale: The Planning DB contained a later reactivation design for SYS-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL, but the declared CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel.tsx and CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel.test.tsx files are not tracked. Existing active files already resolve to SYS-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-OVERLAY and SYS-WEB-CANVAS-INSPECTOR-PANEL. This migration retires the phantom component boundary and redirects the overlay dependency to the real inspector component.

design.title: Restore Canvas node workbench panel authority after post-import legacy rows
design.rationale: The database component profile must point at the real CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel component, not the retired CanvasNodeWorkbenchDuplicateResolution placeholder.

design.title: Reassert Canvas node workbench panel effective profile

design.title: Reactivate Canvas node workbench panel with a real panel component

CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel.tsx now owns the Canvas-specific node workbench presentation while reusing the existing InspectCanvasNodeProperties query read model and ConfigureCanvasDbtNode/ConfigureCanvasDvtNode commands.

design.title: Neutralize Canvas node workbench panel profile reassertion
design.rationale: Superseded by PLANNING-DB-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL-ACTIVE-MERGE-RECONCILIATION-20260619 because tracked CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel source and test files now exist.

design.title: Restore Canvas node workbench panel relations
design.rationale: The active Canvas node workbench panel needs declared contains and overlay dependency relations so architecture maturity evidence matches the implemented files, ports, tests, and feature manifest.

design.title: Harden untracked Canvas node workbench panel reversal
design.rationale: Superseded by PLANNING-DB-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL-ACTIVE-MERGE-RECONCILIATION-20260619 because tracked CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel source and test files now exist.

design.title: Reverse untracked Canvas node workbench panel reactivation
design.rationale: Superseded by PLANNING-DB-WEB-CANVAS-NODE-WORKBENCH-PANEL-ACTIVE-MERGE-RECONCILIATION-20260619 because tracked CanvasNodeWorkbenchPanel source and test files now exist.

design.title: Planning DB Web Canvas Output Target Template Component Map
design.rationale: The Canvas output target template catalog was still owned by the flat residual Canvas bucket. This design records it as a semantic component so component-profile can answer files, tests, rails, DDD/Fowler basis, and relationships.

design.title: Web Canvas parallel test drift reconciliation
design.rationale: Parallel Web Canvas work replaced the monolithic viewport graph-model and legacy-guide tests with split, tracked test files after the Planning DB state had referenced the old surfaces. This design reconciles current DB authority to the real filesystem and records old paths as deprecated excludes instead of recreating stub files.

design.title: Web Canvas residual component split
design.rationale: SYS-WEB-VIEW-CANVAS-RESIDUAL-SURFACES retained most flat Canvas route files. This design creates semantic filesystem-backed Canvas child components so component-profile can answer files, tests, rails, DDD/Fowler basis, and relationships without a side inventory.

design.title: Web Canvas residual surfaces component deprecation
design.rationale: SYS-WEB-VIEW-CANVAS-RESIDUAL-SURFACES owns no files, has no children, exposes no ports, and has no contract evidence after the Web Canvas leaf splits. Keeping it active duplicates the Canvas directory repo_path and weakens component-profile answers. The component is deprecated as a historical residual bucket; live files remain mapped to concrete Canvas child components.

design.title: Web Canvas shell chrome leaf component mapping
design.rationale: SYS-WEB-CANVAS-SHELL-CHROME owned 39 active shell files directly across center-surface rendering, route state, grouped shell composition, graph/chrome command adapters, and menu/drawer contribution responsibilities. This migration keeps the existing component as the aggregate shell chrome boundary and maps concrete files to responsibility-owned leaves with component graph relations, ports, contracts, tests, observability, and Fowler/DDD basis.

design.title: Web Canvas shell chrome parent path canonicalization
design.rationale: Canvas graph and shell aggregates use unique current architecture anchors while shell-chrome leaves own the concrete presentation files.

design.title: Web Canvas source import frame composite
design.rationale: The source import frame is a composite boundary under the source import wizard. The current Planning DB state needs this parent component before frame presentation and test leaves can exist, otherwise child architecture rows depend on local operate-only state.

design.title: Web Canvas source import frame presentation leaf
design.rationale: Once SourceImportSectionTabs tests became a child leaf, the source import frame could no longer own presentation files directly. This design moves its real UI widgets into a presentation leaf while keeping the frame as the composite component.

design.title: Web Canvas source import section tabs test evidence
design.rationale: The SourceImportSectionTabs test leaf needs explicit architecture test evidence after the ownership leaf is created, so component-profile and component-integrity can answer which executable test validates the leaf.

design.title: Web Canvas source import section tabs test leaf
design.rationale: SourceImportSectionTabs.test.tsx was introduced by a parallel Web Canvas/source-import slice and initially resolved to the composite source import wizard. This design creates a focused test leaf under the source import frame so component quality can answer ownership without broad parent claims.

design.title: Web Canvas inspector tabs parent canonicalization
design.rationale: After creating a NodePropertiesTabs presenter leaf, the parent inspector tabs component must stop sharing the same architecture repo_path. The parent is now the composite feature area and the presenter owns the concrete TSX file.

design.title: Web Canvas test evidence command canonicalization
design.rationale: Component profiles exposed test evidence commands that used @dvt/web test, which runs unrelated suites before path filtering. This design authorizes updating the existing TEST-* rows to the focused presentation test rail that was actually validated.

design.title: Web root filesystem leaf component mapping
design.rationale: SYS-WEB-ROOT still owned most apps/web files directly. This design creates filesystem-backed child components and local parent definitions so component-profile can answer files, subcomponents, commands, queries, adapters, ports, tests, docs, and Fowler/DDD ownership without a side inventory.

design.title: Map Web source import catalog view component and retire duplicate rail
design.rationale: The contextual source import branch added SourceImportCatalogView.tsx and SourceImportCatalogView.test.tsx. After integration both files resolved only to SYS-WEB-ROOT while the same slice also left a feature-local ListWarehouseConnectionTables projection that duplicates the canonical implemented warehouse table query. This design maps the active presentation files to a leaf component and retires only the duplicate rail projection.

design.title: Web UI primitive leaf component mapping
design.rationale: SYS-WEB-APP-COMPONENTS-UI owned 50 active shadcn-style primitives directly under apps/web/src/app/components/ui. This migration keeps the existing component as the aggregate design-system primitive boundary and maps concrete files into foundation, form controls, overlays, navigation, feedback, data display, and composition/layout leaves with component graph relations, internal render ports, contracts, tests, observability, and Fowler basis.

design.title: Web views legacy DiffView harness deprecation
design.rationale: apps/web/src/app/views/test/DiffViewHarness.tsx is still present in the Planning DB ownership snapshot but is absent from the repository filesystem. The correct action is to deprecate the historical harness reference, not recreate a stub or leave SYS-WEB-ROOT owning it.

design.title: Workers root leaf component mapping
design.rationale: SYS-WORKERS-ROOT directly owned Lineage, Outbox, Projector, and Temporal worker files. This design maps host, runtime, adapter, ops, ownership, canary, and application responsibilities to explicit leaf components with command/query/event/storage/API ports.

design.title: API governance DB cleanup
design.rationale: Remap current API documentation and semantic test evidence after retiring compiled catalogs and topology-only harnesses.

design.title: API governance residual evidence cleanup
design.rationale: Repoint residual PlanStore test and validation evidence discovered by the pre-push integrity gate.

design.title: API fixture evidence retirement closeout
design.rationale: Replace the last active topology-test validation command with executable workflow-snapshot and workspace-graph behavior evidence.

design.title: API compiled governance retirement
design.rationale: Retire non-runtime TypeScript rail catalogs, topology locks, duplicate test execution and hand-maintained API maps while keeping behavioral boundaries and DB-first architecture authority.

design.title: Architecture design lifecycle closeout
design.rationale: Add an audited lifecycle command so superseded designs and the final implemented design are unambiguous after review.

design.title: DB-first governance ownership closeout
design.rationale: Replace obsolete imported API ownership with audited database overrides and on-demand projections.

design.title: DB-first governance component recovery
design.rationale: Persist audited component overrides and DB surface catalog state through explicit Planning DB export and destructive current-schema rebuild.

design.title: API governance retirement QA closeout
design.rationale: Replace active references to retired compiled governance surfaces with semantic tests, explicit contracts, and DB-first architecture authority.

design.title: API governance validation command closeout
design.rationale: Remove obsolete compiled-governance filenames from active validation commands after their semantic test replacements are authoritative.

design.title: DB-first governance projection closeout
design.rationale: Publish effective governance ownership and navigation-only architecture guidance from Planning DB only through the existing explicit export command, removing stale local inventory authority.

design.title: Classify pull-request authority before check publication
design.rationale: A pure specification classifies trusted pull-request metadata before any checks:write job starts. Same-repository pull requests publish on the exact head SHA; fork product pull requests publish on the base-repository test merge SHA; release candidates remain restricted to same-repository pull requests targeting main.

design.title: One admitted release identity per merged pull request
design.rationale: Release Please only generates the candidate. A trusted coordinator opens the required check on the exact PR head SHA, runs immutable assessment in a separate read-only job, and completes the same check through an application service and GitHub Checks adapter.

design.title: Require one trusted release governance credential
design.rationale: Release candidate generation and full repository-ruleset inspection require an identity outside GITHUB_TOKEN. The workflow must fail before mutation when that identity is absent, and policy projection must reject API responses that omit bypass actors.

design.title: Project merge policy evidence at the workflow boundary
design.rationale: InspectReleasePullRequestMergePolicy returns an evidence envelope while AssessReleaseCandidateIntegrity consumes the nested canonical policy. The trusted workflow is the composition boundary and must perform that explicit projection.

design.title: Shared runs operational truth projection
design.rationale: ListRuns and GetRunStatus currently expose different identity and time shapes, while the browser fabricates startedAt from its local clock. A pure projection must bind persisted run metadata to canonical event-log status once, preserve missing evidence honestly, and feed both query rails without creating a third product query.

design.title: Source Import catalog primitives component boundary
design.rationale: SourceImportCatalogView must remain a presentational composition over the catalog read model. The extracted SourceImportCatalogPrimitives component owns schema headers, table cards, column preview rows and class tokens so the view does not accumulate ad hoc JSX/CSS while preserving the existing warehouse source import rails.

design.title: Trusted pull-request metadata isolation
design.rationale: The PR quality job executes candidate code and therefore remains read-only. File-derived label mutation moves to a trusted pull_request_target adapter, while PR scope assessment reads the immutable base SHA from the shallow merge snapshot without exposing credentials to repository code.

design.title: Web bottom operational drawer vocabulary
design.rationale: The Canvas-first specification moves logs, problems, runs, and execution preview into a bottom operational drawer. BottomConsoleDrawer duplicated outdated console vocabulary and hid the multi-panel product boundary behind a single-purpose implementation name.

design.title: Canvas context menu view-model presenter
design.rationale: CanvasContextMenuView still owned grouping decisions for Add, Canvas, and edge sections. The presenter extraction keeps the React template passive, makes section grouping directly testable, and preserves the existing ResolveCanvasContextMenu rail instead of creating a parallel menu command.

design.title: DBT authoring field section components
design.rationale: DbtAuthoringFields mixed graph-origin projection, generated SQL derivation, form controls, validation copy, and DBT source/model markup in one React file. The split keeps the component database under web.component.canvas.DbtAuthoringFields while extracting pure model logic and source/model presentation leaves so later Canvas-first UX changes can target explicit components instead of ad hoc JSX blocks.

design.title: DBT authoring fields component registration
design.rationale: The focused Canvas component drift query expects DbtAuthoringFields.tsx to belong to web.component.canvas.DbtAuthoringFields. That component was still only represented by older SYS-* inventory rows, so the effective frontend component registry could not join the file mapping. This migration makes DBT authoring fields a database local component before UI behavior work proceeds.

design.title: DVT Canvas authoring field section split
design.rationale: DvtAuthoringFields had accumulated source, SQL transform, and sink presentation branches in one TSX file. The professional Canvas work needs separate presentational leaves so the node workbench can evolve without duplicating field semantics or embedding ad hoc HTML in the selector.

design.title: DVT transform input column selection
design.rationale: DVT transform authoring could edit SQL but could not inspect or select columns from connected source nodes. The professional canvas flow needs the transform section to query upstream source metadata from the graph and persist selected input-column refs through the existing node draft command path.

design.title: Canvas fixed add-node palette retirement
design.rationale: The Canvas-first specification makes the graph the base mode and routes node insertion through the Canvas context menu. CanvasAddNodePalette, its template catalogs, and first-node copy/tests duplicated the ResolveCanvasContextMenu/CreateCanvasAuthoringNode rails and kept fixed insertion chrome alive.

design.title: Canvas node context-menu primitive boundary
design.rationale: CanvasNodeContextMenuView was still carrying Radix menu primitives and CSS token constants. This migration keeps the semantic component as web.component.canvas.CanvasNodeContextMenu while moving low-level presentation templates into CanvasNodeContextMenuPrimitives.tsx and removing legacy constant symbols from the database feature manifest.

design.title: Canvas visual palette token classification
design.rationale: The component registry drift guard incorrectly classified canvasPalette.ts as a legacy fixed add-node palette. The file contains visual color tokens consumed by CanvasViewport and ShellMenu, while the fixed add-node palette path is CanvasAddNodePalette.tsx and is already absent. This migration keeps the legacy sentinel for CanvasAddNodePalette.tsx while mapping visual palette tokens to CanvasViewport.

design.title: Workspace CAS integrity and rail reconciliation
design.rationale: Production-only implementation evidence exposed historical documentation aliases and incomplete component maturity records. The canonical catalog must retain only executable rails and one owner per implementation path.

design.title: Workspace file revision compare-and-swap
design.rationale: GetWorkspaceFileContent and SaveWorkspaceFileContent retain one provider-neutral WorkspaceFileContent owner, revision CAS, protected HTTP adapters, and DB-local command/query authority without a parallel DBT-specific persistence rail.

decision.title: Bind workspace authorization scope to physical storage scope
decision.rationale: Authorization without matching storage partitioning permits cross-workspace data disclosure and incorrect dbt bundle construction.

decision.title: dbt project authoring authority
decision.rationale: Each Canvas has exactly one semantic authority. Graph-draft and dbt-project-files use separate aggregates or projections and never persist ignored shadow graph semantics.
